paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The LORD doesn't hand Job an explanation. He hands him a view. He asks, "Do you have an arm like God's? Can you thunder with a voice like His?" (Job 40:9), and then He shows Job Behemoth and Leviathan, two creatures Job can't tame, and says, "Then who is able to stand against Me?" (Job 41:10).

Now watch what that does. The LORD says, "Everything under heaven is Mine." (Job 41:11). Nobody is running this world better than He is, and nobody is holding it together but Him. Job spent a lot of this book trying to figure out how God was running things. I spent years in a junk drawer sure I knew how my story ended, and I was WRONG, friend. Being the one who is NOT in charge is a relief, if the One in charge is good.

And that's what Job finds. He says, "My ears had heard of You, but now my eyes have seen You." (Job 42:5). His answers didn't change first. His view of God did. So when life doesn't make sense, baker, don't just chase the why. Look for Him, because knowing Him is bigger than any answer you could ask for.
